ProResp
Sponsored
Fifteen years ago, the doctors told Stacy and Tyler that their prematurely born son was not going to make it. Stacy and Tyler had other ideas. They knew that Kayne, which is Gaelic for “little battler,” would put up a fight. 

In 2008, when Stacy was in her 28th week of pregnancy, she was diagnosed with HELLP syndrome and sent for an emergency caesarian section. Kayne was born weighing barely 2 pounds. 

For his first 8 months, Kayne lived in the hospital hooked up to a ventilator. Doctors did not expect him to make it, so Stacy and Tyler decided to bring him home. Kayne was released on palliative care on May 5, 2009 with ProResp assigned to help keep him comfortable for as long as possible.

“I was 24. It was hard to imagine past the reality of what we were living. I just knew I had this little miracle, and I was determined to treat him like any healthy newborn, with the smiles and happiness that all babies deserve,” Stacy told us.

At first, ProResp visited every day. “They were there to support us with everything. They came on our first walk, were there to help us wean him off the ventilator and to walk us through his first tracheostomy tube change. You don’t think you are going to have baby milestones like the ones we had with Kayne and ProResp, but as a team we made sure he had the best quality of life possible,” Stacy recalled.

By September 2010, Kayne was off the ventilator and by January 2011, his tracheostomy tube was removed. He still got sick more often than most kids, but against all odds, Kayne was pulling through. 

Today, Kayne is a 16-year-old kid with hobbies and interests that include playing the guitar. Recently, he bought a matte black Johnny Cash style guitar that he is absolutely thrilled with. 

“ProResp essentially gave us life,” Stacy said. “When Kayne came home he was not supposed to make it. We are so thankful for all the things they’ve done. He is who he is because of the community of people who got him here.”

Stories like these are the reason we became Respiratory Therapists. Thank you, Stacy, Tyler and Kayne, for sharing your incredibly moving experience; we are so thankful that Kayne now tells his story. 

Learn more at prorespcares.ca

Baby Acrobatics
Sponsored
There’s 4 truths you need to understand…

1️⃣ Milestones are outputs. What matters is the reps that come before them

2️⃣ Movement wires the brain. Stillness doesn’t

3️⃣ Containers are for transport, not development

4️⃣ Confidence builds from safe freedom, not restriction

So here’s how you multiply quality movement without adding time…

🍼 For younger babies (0–4 months):
⏱️ Micro-sessions — 5 × 3 minutes: side-lying reach → roll, diagonal hip lifts, prone weight-shifts over forearms.
❤️ Tummy-time alternatives — chest-to-chest on you, over your forearm, or with a small towel under the chest.
↔️ Fix asymmetry — give two extra reps to the side they avoid.
🎢 Vestibular — slow tilts, gentle swings, brief supported upside-down peeks (stop if fussing).

🚼 For mid-stage babies (4–8 months):
🖐️ Hands first — load open palms on the floor or your forearm to prep wrists and shoulders.
🧭 Ratio — aim 2 : 1 floor time vs. container time across the day.
🏡 Yes-space — firm surface, thin rug for traction, a few low cushions to crawl over, stable furniture edge to pull to stand.
🦶 Gear — barefoot or grippy socks; skip slippery fabrics so traction stays real.

🚶 For older babies (8 months +):
🧺 Containers with off-ramps — car seat for the car, then floor; babywear for connection, then floor.
🎯 Mini obstacle play — pillows, tunnels, boxes to crawl through and over.
🏗️ Early standing work — let them cruise along a sofa edge or your thighs.
🪁 Controlled wobble — balance on your lap, gentle side shifts, soft landings.

Every baby deserves movement freedom, every parent deserves a simple plan.

That’s exactly what the Baby Acrobatics Blueprint gives you—daily 15-minute sequences, progressions, and spotting cues you can follow step by step.

Kayne was born weighing barely 2 pounds. \n\nFor his first 8 months, Kayne lived in the hospital hooked up to a ventilator. Doctors did not expect him to make it, so Stacy and Tyler decided to bring him home. Kayne was released on palliative care on May 5, 2009 with ProResp assigned to help keep him comfortable for as long as possible.\n\n\u201cI was 24. It was hard to imagine past the reality of what we were living. I just knew I had this little miracle, and I was determined to treat him like any healthy newborn, with the smiles and happiness that all babies deserve,\u201d Stacy told us.\n\nAt first, ProResp visited every day. \u201cThey were there to support us with everything. They came on our first walk, were there to help us wean him off the ventilator and to walk us through his first tracheostomy tube change. You don\u2019t think you are going to have baby milestones like the ones we had with Kayne and ProResp, but as a team we made sure he had the best quality of life possible,\u201d Stacy recalled.\n\nBy September 2010, Kayne was off the ventilator and by January 2011, his tracheostomy tube was removed.
